newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt open on special Telstra div.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt open on special Telstra div.

text.p: Australian Communications Minister Richard Alston on Tuesday would not rule out receiving a special dividend from state telecoms giant Telstra Corp ahead of its partial privatisation later this year.
Asked by reporters if he expected a one-off dividend from Telstra, Alston said: "We'll worry about that a little later."
The Australian Financial Review newspaper reported on Monday that Telstra would pay the government a special dividend of up to A$3 billion.
The Financial Review, quoting senior Telstra officials, said the timing and amount of the payment were yet to be determined.
The government plans to sell one-third of the domestic and international telecommunications firm by the end of calendar 1997, raising more than A$8 billion.

Telstra on Friday announced a 16.1 percent jump in net profit before abnormals to A$1.40 billion for the six months to December 31 and an interim dividend to the government of A$625 million. However, Telstra booked an abnormal loss of A$1.026 billion related to estimated redundancies and restructuring costs.
